title: Masked machine step correspondence
statement: Let $A$ be an alphabet, $W$ a finite Turing machine over $A$, $z\in A$, $x$ a finite input word, and $c$ a configuration of $W$ on $x$. Regard $c$ as a configuration on the constant word consisting of $|x|$ copies of $z$, preserving its state, input-head position, work tapes and heads, and output. Then masking the result of one step of the masked machine from $c$ gives exactly the result of one step of $W$ from the masked configuration of $c$, including when $c$ is halted.
hypotheses_covered: W is a finite Turing machine over A
z is a symbol in A
x is a finite word over A
c is a configuration on x
replaced:
Let $W$ be a machine over an alphabet $A$, let $z \in A$, and let $c$ be a
configuration of the masked clock of $W$ on an input word $x$. Masking the result of
one step of the masked clock at $c$ yields the same configuration as performing one
step of $W$ at the masked configuration of $c$; this includes the absorbing case in
which $c$ is already halted.
